name: shader-color-panels
title: Shader Color Panels
description: Translucent color panels swing through depth and slide past each other: a glassy, architectural WebGL backdrop in any palette.
useWhen: You want an architectural, glassy backdrop of translucent panes sliding past each other.
A scene benefits from layered depth without organic blob motion; tune the panel count with `density`.
avoidWhen: You want organic, flowing motion: use shader-warp or shader-metaballs.
The overlapping panes would clutter dense foreground content: lower `density`.
You need a single smooth gradient: use shader-mesh-gradient.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Colors
variables.description: Up to 7 colors, comma separated, one per panel in turn.

variables.label: Speed
variables.description: How fast the panels swing past. 0 holds still.

variables.label: Density
variables.description: How many panels are in view at once.

variables.label: Blur
variables.description: Softens the panel edges, more toward the front.

variables.label: Gradient
variables.description: Blends each panel into the next color along its length.

variables.label: Scale
variables.description: Zooms the scene in or out.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Lower renders faster; this soft look holds at 0.5.
